'''John Paul Hempel''' (October 14, 1935 &ndash; January 13, 2022<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Obituary of John Paul Hempel {{!}} Anderson-McQueen - N.E. St. Petersburg Family Tribute Center |url=https://andersonmcqueen.com/tribute/details/255017/John-Hempel/obituary.html |access-date=2022-04-21 |website=andersonmcqueen.com |language=en-US}}</ref>) was an American mathematician specialising in [[geometric topology]].

== Early life and career ==
Hempel was born in [[Salt Lake City]], Utah. In 1957 he graduated from the [[University of Utah]] with a [[Mathematics|degree in mathematics]]. In 1962, he defended his thesis at the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]], under the supervision of [[R. H. Bing]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=684}}</ref> He was a professor at [[Rice University]] until the time of his death.<ref name=":0" />

In 2013, Hempel was elected a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=http://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

==Research==
He also introduced the study of the [[curve complex]] into 3-manifold topology.<ref>{{cite journal| last=Hempel | first=John | title=3-manifolds as viewed from the curve complex | journal=[[Topology (journal)|Topology]] | volume=40 | number=3 | pages=631–657 | year=2001 | doi=10.1016/S0040-9383(00)00033-1 |zbl=0985.57014 | s2cid=16532184 | doi-access=free | arxiv=math/9712220 }}</ref>

Hempel wrote a book about [[3-manifold]]s in 1976.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hempel |first=John |title=3-Manifolds |date=1976 |publisher=Princeton University Press|series=Annals of Mathematics Studies|volume=86 |isbn=978-0-8218-6939-0 |language=en}} Reprinted 2004 by AMS Chelsea Publishing, {{doi|10.1090/chel/349}}. Reviews:
*{{Cite journal |last=Scott |first=G. P. |date=November 1977 |title=none |journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=345–346 |doi=10.1112/blms/9.3.345}}
*[[Joan Birman|J. S. Birman]], {{MR|0415619}}
*F. Waldhausen, {{zbl|0345.57001}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He was married to Edith, whom he married on September 1, 1965, in [[Houston]], Texas; they had one son.<ref name=":0" />
